title: Redridge Mountains
body: The Redridge Mountains rise east of Elwynn Forest, a land of red stone ridges and wooded slopes gathered around the long waters of Lake Everstill, and all of it sovereign land of the King of Stormwind. Orcs have scarred these hills before: the Horde overran them in the First War, and Lakeshire was rebuilt only after the Second. Now war has returned. Blackrock orcs out of the Burning Steppes, aided by the dark magic of a renegade warlock named Morganth, have seized Stonewatch Keep and raid everything north of Lakeshire. Morganth himself holds the Tower of Ilgalar in the east, and the Shadowhide gnolls do his bidding. Redridge gnolls prowl the hills and the southern road, murlocs crowd the lakeshore, and the Everstill Bridge waits to be rebuilt. Magistrate Solomon pleads with Stormwind for soldiers, and in the meantime Lakeshire holds on with a handful of guards and whatever help passes through.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Redridge_Mountains (location, First War, Blackrock and Morganth seize the east and Stonewatch)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Lakeshire (taken in the First War, rebuilt after the Second)
quest 20 description (Blackrocks from the Burning Steppes, citizens penned in town)
quest 128 description (sovereign right of the King of Stormwind)
notes: Converted: Morganth turning on the orcs dropped from the opening (Theocritus discovers the quarrel in quest 248; told in 4418 part 1 and 4424 part 2), and 'none have come' softened to Solomon pleading for soldiers, since the army's failure to come is the Letters chain (4422). No parts. Red stone and wooded slopes is scene-setting from the zone's look, not a sourced claim.

title: Three Corners
body: Three Corners is the crossroads just inside the western edge of Redridge, where the road from Elwynn Forest divides, one way running northeast to Lakeshire and the other south toward Darkshire in Duskwood, so that the three shires of the kingdom meet here. In quieter years it needed little watching, and a single Stormwind guard, Guard Parker, still walks the stretch of road toward Duskwood. He has lately spotted gnoll encampments gathering to the north and east, not far from the Elwynn border. Tarantulas and Redridge mongrels lurk beside the roads, and a gnoll known as Ribchaser roams among them.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Three_Corners (crossroads to the three shires, quiet, patrolled by Guard Parker pre-Cataclysm)
quest 129 description (Parker patrols the road leading to Duskwood)
DB: Guard Parker 464 at map 15,72; areaId 1002 holds Redridge Mongrel, Tarantula, Ribchaser 14271
notes: Converted: Lakeshire's fear that the gnolls may push into the heartland is Deputy Feldon's reaction on the turn-in of 244; dropped here and told in 4425 part 1. No parts. Tower Watch at the crossroads is a Cataclysm addition and is left out.

title: Lakeridge Highway
body: The Lakeridge Highway follows the southern shore of Lake Everstill across Redridge. It was once a well traveled road, but traffic dwindled after the orcs took Stonewatch Keep, and today gnolls hold much of its length. Deputy Feldon of Lakeshire, with no men of his own to spare, sends volunteers to harry the mongrels and poachers camped along the southern road and to count their numbers. Condors circle above the ridges, and black dragon whelps flit through the country south of Lakeshire, hunted by the town smith for their tough underbelly scales.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Lakeridge_Highway (road along the south of the lake, fell into disuse after Stonewatch fell, gnolls)
DB: areaId 1001 holds Redridge Mongrel, Redridge Poacher, Dire Condor, Black Dragon Whelp
notes: Converted: the grim count of the gnoll force is Feldon's verdict on the turn-in of 246; dropped here and told in 4425 part 2. No parts. The fossil dig site on the wiki page is Cataclysm archaeology and is left out.

title: Lakeshire
body: Lakeshire is the heart of Redridge, a town on the western shore of Lake Everstill. Taken by the Horde in the First War and rebuilt after the Second, it is under siege once again. Magistrate Solomon presides over the Court of Lakeshire from the town hall, Marshal Marris directs its few soldiers, and Verner Osgood keeps the stable and the forge. The inn stays open even as its bottles run dry, sheltering townsfolk and shadier guests, among them a rogue called Wiley who owes Gryan Stoutmantle a favor. The Everstill Bridge, which carries the road into town from the south, was blown out in the fighting, and Foreman Oslow's crew labors to rebuild it with scarce iron.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Lakeshire (history, town hall and Court, inn)
DB spawns: Solomon 344 at 30,44; Marris 382 and Oslow 341 at the bridge 32-34,49; Guard Howe at 31.5,58
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified

title: Lake Everstill
body: Lake Everstill fills the center of Redridge, its eastern river spilling down past Stonewatch toward the falls. The lake is famous for its spotted sunfish, but larger bands of murlocs have begun dropping anchor along its shores and fishing it bare, strangely far from the sea, as though something had driven them inland. Much has sunk beneath its surface. When orc catapults struck a boat carrying Foreman Oslow's toolbox, the box went straight to the bottom, and a little girl fishing from the Lakeshire docks lost her father's gift of a necklace to the water. The townsfolk warn their children of mean things below, and a great beast called the Lake Thresher prowls the deeps.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Lake_Everstill (center of Redridge, eastern river, murlocs, Lake Thresher)
DB: Lake Thresher 14357 and murlocs in areaId 68; Hilary 8962 and Shawn 8965 at the docks
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. The murlocs seeming to flee something is Wilm's musing (quest 150 reward text), not an outcome. The wiki's portal and drought tale is left out (no period source).

title: Redridge Canyons
body: North of Lakeshire the land climbs into the Redridge Canyons, a tangle of ridges and ravines where the Redridge gnolls make their home. Brutes and mystics prowl the ridge above Verner Osgood's stable and carry off any horse that strays, and the pack's baying drifts down to the town at night. Loudest of all is Yowler, the pack leader, who keeps his den in the canyons and is a far more dangerous foe than the mongrels who follow him. When a shipment of iron bound from Stormwind for the Everstill Bridge was hijacked, it was these gnolls who dragged it off into the hills behind the town.
sources: DB: Yowler 518, Redridge Brute, Mystic, Basher, Alpha in areaId 95
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified

title: Rethban Caverns
body: The Rethban Caverns open in the foothills north of Lakeshire, named for Bart Rethban, the man who first found ore there. Rethban ore smelts weaker than iron, but its dark, flat color is prized by scribes who blend it into their dyes, and Lakeshire usually kept a supply. That has changed. Redridge gnolls have moved into the caverns, and their drudgers now dig the ore for themselves. The dwarf Yorus Barleybrew of the Lakeshire Inn has made the tunnels a test of nerve, the Rethban Gauntlet: a run to the first fork and back within the hour, through heaps of gnolls, after a swig of his family's Barleybrew Scalder.
sources: quest 347 description (Bart Rethban, ore, gnoll drudgers)
DB: Redridge Drudger 580 and Redridge Alpha 445 in areaId 98
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified

title: Render's Camp
body: Where the road climbs out of Redridge toward the Burning Steppes, the Blackrock clan has made camp just west of the pass. From Render's Camp the champions who lead each Blackrock unit direct the war on Lakeshire, trackers range the slopes around it, and an orc called Kazon is sometimes seen among them. Within the camp lies Render's Rock, a large cave held by powerful Blackrock warriors. It was here that the orcs dragged Corporal Keeshan, taken alive in the bloody battle at Stonewatch Keep, to hold him as a prisoner of war.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Render's_Camp (Blackrock outpost near the Burning Steppes entrance)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Render's_Rock (large cave, powerful Blackrock orcs, Keeshan)
DB: Blackrock Champion 435 in areaId 998, Blackrock Tracker 615 in 996/998, Kazon 584 at 35,8, Keeshan 349 at 28,13
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Covers both areas 996 and 998, since Render's Rock is a subzone of the camp. Fact-checked: verified.

title: Alther's Mill
body: Northeast of Lakeshire, just off the road to Stonewatch, stands Alther's Mill, an abandoned lumber mill. Most travelers pass it on their way east without stopping. Greater tarantulas have overrun the old timberworks, among them a monstrous spider called Chatter, and a black whelp named Snarlflare has been seen in the area. The quiet suits some. An associate of SI:7 who loiters on the Lakeshire docks has trained young thieves here for years, keeping lockboxes at the mill for them to crack, though he admits orcs have lately been seen nosing around the place.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Alther's_Mill (abandoned lumber mill northeast of Lakeshire, travelers pass through)
quest 2281 description (Lucius, SI:7 associate, at the docks)
DB: Chatter 616 (spider), Greater Tarantula 505, Snarlflare 14272, Practice Lockbox 178246 in areaId 97
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Who Alther was is unknown and not guessed at. The Blackrock worg kennel on the wiki is later content and left out. Fact-checked: verified.

title: Stonewatch Falls
body: East of Stonewatch, the river that drains Lake Everstill tumbles down the slope and gathers in a deep pool in a hollow of the eastern mountains. A small band of murlocs fishes the pool and sleeps in rough shelters along its banks. The falls are no refuge, though. Blackrock outrunners and renegades, the raiders who ambush travelers on the roads between Lakeshire and the keep, range across the slopes here, and Shadowhide warriors from the valley to the north are never far away.
sources: quest 19 description (outrunners and renegades ambush between Lakeshire and Stonewatch)
DB: areaId 71 holds Murloc Nightcrawler 544, Blackrock Outrunner 485, Blackrock Renegade 437, Shadowhide Warrior 568
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified

title: Stonewatch Keep
body: Stonewatch Keep once belonged to the people of Lakeshire. Then the Blackrock orcs came over the mountains from the Burning Steppes, and with the dark magic of the warlock Morganth behind them they stormed the keep. Most of the regiment that fought there was slain, and Corporal Keeshan was dragged away a prisoner. Now Warlord Gath'Ilzogg has made the keep his stronghold, plotting the clan's next raids from within, while sentries, gladiators and shadowcasters bearing demon-tainted midnight orbs guard its halls. Beside it stands Stonewatch Tower, the one watch tower still intact, where the orcs keep scouts and summoners.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Stonewatch_Keep (held by Lakeshire, taken by Gath'Ilzogg with Morganth's magic)
quest 219 description (regiment overpowered, most men killed)
quest 248 description (intact watch tower beside Stonewatch Keep)

title: Galardell Valley
body: Galardell Valley runs through the eastern foothills of Redridge, and it belongs to the Shadowhide gnolls. The Shadowhide answer to a master, the warlock Morganth, who speaks to them through the enchanted pendants they wear. Their camps crowd the valley under the command of Lieutenant Fangore, the strongest of them, and some of the clan have gone rabid. Lakeshire shows them no mercy. By the Law of Lakeshire, aiding a criminal of the kingdom is punishable by death, and the town's bailiff has ordered every Shadowhide gnoll that serves Morganth hunted down.
sources: quest 178 description (pendants as communication with Morganth)
DB: Fangore 703, Shadowhide Gnoll, Brute, Warrior, Rabid Shadowhide Gnoll 434 in areaId 1000
quest 91 description (gnolls aiding Morganth must be killed)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Fact-checked: the bailiff's order is to kill the gnolls (quest 91), not a declaration of outlawry; reworded.

title: Tower of Ilgalar
body: At the eastern edge of Redridge stands the Tower of Ilgalar, a mage tower now claimed by Morganth. Banished from Stormwind for embracing the dark arts, he carried off a powerful tome, Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic, and keeps it in his library here while Stormwind's mages plot to win it back. Shadowhide darkweavers stand guard on the grounds and demonic servants roam the halls, among displays of dragon bones that hint at some study of dragons. Nearby, an old lion statue has kept lonely watch over the tower for decades.
sources: quest 94 description and request text (Lion Statue)
DB: Servant of Ilgalar 819 (demon), Shadowhide Darkweaver 429 in areaId 96; gameobject 103628 Ur's Treatise in area 96; Old Lion Statue 31 at 84,47

notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Fact-checked: 'purpose no one has guessed' was unsourced; now follows the wiki note that the tower's artifacts suggest a study of dragons.

title: Render's Valley
body: In the southeastern pocket of Redridge, below the mountains that divide it from the Swamp of Sorrows, lies Render's Valley, a second Blackrock encampment far from the main host to the north. Grunts and summoners hold its camps, and Lakeshire has ordered them hunted as surely as those at Stonewatch. Not everyone in the valley is an orc. In one camp sits a captured servant of the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest, who still trades in fine tailoring supplies with any traveler who reaches him.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Render's_Valley (southeastern Blackrock outpost, Captured Servant of Azora, pass to Swamp of Sorrows)
quest 20 description (more Blackrocks in the southeastern pocket)
DB: Blackrock Grunt 440 and Summoner 4463 in areaId 997; Captured Servant of Azora 3096 at 74,80
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified

title: Magistrate Solomon
body: Magistrate Solomon is the elected leader of Lakeshire and judge of its court, which sits in the town hall. With orcs at Stonewatch and gnolls in every hill, the township is under constant siege, and Solomon is certain that without reinforcements it will face defeat. He has written his most urgent report to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind, begging for soldiers. Meanwhile he posts bounties on the kingdom's enemies, from the Blackrock warlord at Stonewatch to the gnoll lieutenant of Galardell Valley, and enforces the Law of Lakeshire against all who aid them.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Magistrate_Solomon (elected ruler, judge of the Court of Lakeshire)
notes: Converted: the general's promise and Solomon's unease moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 121, turned in to Solomon); the refusals from Westfall and Darkshire and his suspicion of treachery moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 146, the chain's end). The full exchange is story 4422. Faction 1: Solomon uses faction template 12 (Stormwind). The Burning Steppes True Masters chain to Bolvar and Lady Prestor has no quest givers in this database and is left out. Check: 'warm but empty' in part 1 judged the promise before the army's failure is shown (146); now 'warm', with Solomon's unease carrying the doubt. Opening's report 'has gone' changed to 'he has written', since a newcomer is the one who carries it.

parts.body: The general's answer was warm: Solomon's words carried great weight, the king would be consulted, and reinforcements would march as soon as His Majesty gave word. Yet Solomon found the letter something of a mystery. Something is amiss in the kingdom, he confided, and he feared this was the beginning of the conflict, not its end.
sources: quest 120 reward text (General Marcus Jonathan's reply)

parts.body: No soldiers came. Solomon turned next to Gryan Stoutmantle's People's Militia in Westfall and to Lord Ebonlocke's Night Watch in Darkshire, only to learn that Stormwind's army had abandoned them as well. The discovery shook him. He now speaks openly of treachery, and he means to get to the bottom of whatever is amiss in Stormwind.

title: Marshal Marris
body: Marshal Marris commands the defense of Lakeshire, keeping his post by the Everstill Bridge. His orders are simple: Blackrock orcs are to be hunted wherever they are found, from the heights of Stonewatch to the southeastern pocket of the mountains. He has put a price on Tharil'zun, leader of the outrunners who ambush the roads, and wants the shadowcasters' demon-tainted midnight orbs taken and destroyed. It is Marris who rewards anyone who brings Corporal Keeshan home from the Blackrock camp. He found a moment, too, to name the troublesome local boar: Bellygrub.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Marshal_Marris (near the bridge, wants the orcs and Tharil'zun killed)
DB: Marris 382 at 33.5,49, beside Foreman Oslow at the bridge
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Faction 1: Marris uses faction template 12 (Stormwind, hostile to Horde). Fact-checked: which end of the bridge he stands at is inferred from coordinates only, so the text now says only that he is by the bridge (wiki, DB 33.5,49 beside Oslow).

title: Corporal Keeshan
body: Corporal Keeshan of the 12th Sabre Regiment was at Stonewatch Keep when the Blackrock orcs overran it. Most of his comrades died in the fighting. Keeshan took a heavy blow to the head and woke a prisoner, dragged off to the Blackrock encampment at Render's Rock near the pass to the Burning Steppes. A notice in Lakeshire lists him as missing. Badly hurt and unable to escape alone, he waits in the cave for any friend of the Alliance who might help him back to town, where he means to report to Marshal Marris for duty.
sources: creature_text 349 (12th Sabre Regiment, reporting for duty)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. His rescue is told in story 4423 part 1. creature_text 349 reread: period lines only. Faction 1: Keeshan uses faction template 11 (Stormwind) and quest 219 is Alliance only. His later Bravo Company career, his wife Jade and all Cataclysm material are deliberately absent.

title: Gath'Ilzogg
body: Gath'Ilzogg, Warlord of the Blackrock Clan, led the orc assault on Stonewatch Keep and the raids that have kept Lakeshire penned in ever since. Backed by the warlock Morganth's magic, his warriors took the keep, and he has made it his stronghold, plotting the clan's next blows with a black dragon whelp named Singe at his side. Many innocent people have died in his battles. His supreme executioner, Targorr the Dread, tortured captured defenders on a whim until he was taken and locked in the Stormwind Stockade, where a noble's intervention has kept him from the headsman. Lakeshire offers a handsome reward for the warlord's head.
sources: DB: Gath'Ilzogg 334 and Singe 335 together in Stonewatch Keep
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Targorr in the Stockade is the premise of quest 386 (a Stockade quest, not used as a trigger); the warlord's fall is told in 4423 part 2. creature_text 334 reread: battle cries only. His Cataclysm return as a death knight is left out. The wiki's guess that Singe was a gift from Nefarius is left out.

title: Morganth
body: Morganth was once one of three mages who studied together in Stormwind, until he fell to the dark arts. Urged to turn away from them, he could not, and he was banished, taking with him a powerful tome, Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. He settled in the Tower of Ilgalar in eastern Redridge and lent his magic to the Blackrock orcs in their assault on Stonewatch Keep. The Shadowhide gnolls of Galardell Valley now do his bidding, taking his commands through enchanted pendants, and Lakeshire calls him an enemy of the kingdom. In Elwynn Forest, his rival Theocritus watches him from afar.
sources: quest 1938 description (three mages, fall, banishment, the treatise)
DB: Morganth 397 at 80,50 in the tower
notes: Converted: 'turned on his allies' moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 248, whose text first tells of the conflict with the orcs, and keeps it a mystery); the Scythe of Elune moved to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 249, an entry trigger as before, so it shows together with the opening on that route); his death added as part 3 (KILL 397 or QUEST_DONE 249), trimmed to what the kill alone tells. Quests call him both mage (94) and warlock (249, wiki lead); the entry calls him a warlock who trained as a mage, which fits quest 1938. His Cataclysm replacement, Grand Magus Doane, is left out. Check: part 3 trimmed of 'whatever schemes he nursed ended with him', which neither the kill nor quest 249 tells. Opening checked: the fall and banishment come from quest 1938 (a separate Stormwind mage quest), his help taking Stonewatch from the wiki and the zone's own premise, and his command of the gnolls from quests 91 and 178, all offered before or outside the Theocritus chain; nothing in it is first told by 94, 248 or 249.

parts.body: The alliance that took Stonewatch has soured. Peering into the Tower of Ilgalar through the Eye of Azora, Theocritus has seen that Morganth is now in conflict with the orcs of the keep, though the cause of their quarrel is still a mystery to him.
sources: quest 248 description (Morganth is in conflict with the Orcs in Stonewatch Keep)

parts.body: Further watching uncovered the warlock's purpose. Morganth searches for the Scythe of Elune, and Theocritus fears he may already have found it. If so, the high mage warns, Redridge and the whole kingdom of Stormwind will soon feel his dark might, and though he is not prepared to face his rival himself, he judges that Morganth must be dealt with now.

Morganth fell at last in the Tower of Ilgalar, struck down among the demonic servants that roam its halls. The banished mage who lent his sorcery to the conquest of Stonewatch, and who bent the Shadowhide gnolls of Galardell Valley to his will, is dead.
sources: quest 249 reward text (in defeating the warlock Morganth)
DB: Servant of Ilgalar 819 in areaId 96

title: Lieutenant Fangore
body: Lieutenant Fangore leads the Shadowhide gnoll clan in Morganth's name and is the strongest of the gnolls who prowl Galardell Valley. Lakeshire counts him a traitor to Stormwind as much as a beast, and a wanted poster in town, issued by mandate of Magistrate Solomon, calls for his death with his paw as proof. Fangore is cunning as well as fierce. He seldom fights alone, and those who corner him often find the rest of his pack answering his call.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Galardell_Valley (strongest gnoll, calls others for help)
DB: Fangore 703 in areaId 1000; poster gameobject 47 in Lakeshire
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. His Cataclysm title of General is left out. Fact-checked: verified.

title: Tharil'zun
body: Tharil'zun leads the Blackrock outrunners, the swift raiders who, with renegades at their side, spring ambushes along the roads between Lakeshire and Stonewatch Keep. He is a vicious and crafty orc who stays close to the keep, and when cornered he flies into a rage. Marshal Marris has called for his head, for while Tharil'zun lives no traveler on the eastern roads is safe.
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. creature_text 486 is only the enrage emote. His Cataclysm return as a death knight is left out.

title: Verner Osgood
body: Verner Osgood runs the stable in Lakeshire and works as the town's blacksmith, and he never has enough iron. Outfitting the Stormwind guards has used so much that he cannot shoe his own horses, and he has written to Smith Argus of Goldshire for a shipment of horseshoes. Gnolls on the ridge above his stable steal any horse that strays, and their leader Yowler howls in the hills. Verner is sure the army, busy with the orcs, has no soldiers to spare for the gnolls.
sources: quest 1618 reward text (fixing armor and making weapons for the troops)
notes: Converted: Argus's bill slipped in with the horseshoes moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 119, turned in to Verner, where he finds the note); the opening keeps his request (quest 118). Quests 118 and 119 are sorted under Redridge and no other file uses them. Faction 1: Verner uses faction template 12 (Stormwind). Check: 'Verner knows no soldiers will come' reframed as his belief (quest 126 reward text), so it does not state the army's absence as fact ahead of the Letters chain.

parts.body: The horseshoes came, fifty of them boxed in a crate from Goldshire, and with them a note from Argus asking to be paid. Verner was indignant, but he means to settle the debt in the tough underbelly scales of the black dragon whelps that wander south of Lakeshire, with enough left over to fashion something for whoever gathers them.

title: Letters from Lakeshire
body: Lakeshire is under constant siege. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch Keep, gnolls prowl the hills, and the town defends itself with only a handful of guards. Magistrate Solomon is certain that without reinforcements it will face defeat, and he has written his most urgent report to General Marcus Jonathan of Stormwind, begging for soldiers. The message is of the utmost importance. Whoever carries it must put it in the general's hands and return to Lakeshire at once with whatever news he gives, be it good or bad.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 120. Parts follow the chain: 1 the general's promise (QUEST_DONE 120, turned in to him in Stormwind; 120 is sorted under Redridge and no other file uses it), 2 Solomon's unease and the turn to Westfall (QUEST_DONE 121), 3 Stoutmantle's refusal (QUEST_DONE 144, turned in to Solomon), 4 Ebonlocke's refusal and the suspicion of treachery (QUEST_DONE 146). Kept consistent with Westfall: its People's Militia entry 4023 keeps only the plea and leaves Stoutmantle's reply to this entry; 143 and 144 are used by no Westfall entry. Faction 1: all six quests are Alliance only. Check: the army's failure to arrive and the letter to Westfall come from quest 143's description, not the 121 turn-in, so they moved out of part 2 into a new part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 143, offered by Solomon once 121 is done; QuestType 2, flags 0). Part 2 keeps Solomon's unease (121 reward text); Stoutmantle and Ebonlocke are now parts 4 and 5. Stoutmantle's reply agrees with Westfall 4023, which keeps only the plea.

parts.body: The general received the report kindly. Solomon was a noble leader, he said, whose words carried great weight, and he would seek the counsel of the king and make the situation plain. Lakeshire had the army's support, and reinforcements would march as soon as word was given from His Majesty. Until then he sent a letter back to the magistrate.

Back in Lakeshire, Solomon read the general's letter and found it something of a mystery. Something was amiss in the kingdom, he said, and he feared this was the beginning of the conflict, not its end. He thanked the messenger for the service to Lakeshire and Stormwind, and waited for the king's word.

The army should have been there in force by then, and still it did not come. Unwilling to stand by while the people of Lakeshire gave their lives, Solomon looked elsewhere for help. Word had reached him of a people's militia forming in Westfall, and he wrote to its leader, Gryan Stoutmantle, asking for men until the king sent reserves.

Stoutmantle's reply was heavy. The magistrate, he wrote, could not know the war being waged in Westfall, or he would not look to the militia for aid: had Stormwind not deserted Westfall too, there would be no need for a militia at all, and his heart was heavy with the loss of good men. Solomon was dismayed to find Stoutmantle's plight so like his own, and asked what could call the army away from its own people. He wrote next to Lord Ebonlocke of Darkshire, asking for the Night Watch.

Ebonlocke's answer was the same. Had he not known Solomon, he wrote, he would think the man mad: the Night Watch was formed because Stormwind left Duskwood when foul magic seeped into the land, and if it marched, Darkshire would be overrun before the guards reached the forest's edge. The army had retreated from Westfall and no longer guarded Darkshire. Solomon now suspects treachery, and he means to discover what is amiss in Stormwind.

title: The Blackrock War
body: The Blackrock orcs came over the mountains from the Burning Steppes and, with Morganth's sorcery to aid them, overwhelmed the defenders of Stonewatch Keep. Since then they have raided everything north of Lakeshire and kept its people penned in town like cattle. Until Stormwind's army arrives, Lakeshire's leaders turn to any willing sword. Marshal Marris pays for the battleworn axes of slain orcs, hunts the outrunner chief Tharil'zun, and wants the shadowcasters' midnight orbs gathered and destroyed. Guard Howe calls for the champions who lead each Blackrock unit at their camp near the pass, and a wanted poster names Warlord Gath'Ilzogg himself, holed up in the conquered keep. Somewhere in the cave at Render's Rock, a wounded Corporal Keeshan waits for rescue.
notes: Converted: the warlord's fall and Solomon's verdict moved from the opening to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 169). Keeshan's return added as part 1 (QUEST_DONE 219, turned in to Marris), since the opening leaves him waiting for rescue. Faction 1: all quests Alliance only. Check: opening's 'with no army coming' (the outcome of the Letters chain, 4422) changed to 'until Stormwind's army arrives', present tense. Part 1 checked against the escort script: Keeshan walks all the way to Marris and reports there; Marris's thanks reworded to fit quest 219's reward text, which praises the helper.

parts.body: Keeshan made it home. Wounded and slow, he was helped out of the Blackrock cave and past the orc camps to Lakeshire, where he stood before Marshal Marris and reported for duty, a soldier of the 12th Sabre Regiment returned from battle. Marris counted the help given in his escape a fine service to the kingdom.
sources: creature_text 349 (wounds, reporting for duty to Marshal Marris)
script npc_corporal_keeshan: escort ends at waypoint 115 beside Marshal Marris (spawn -9284,-2298), where Keeshan reports

parts.body: In time the warlord himself fell. When Gath'Ilzogg's head was laid before Magistrate Solomon, the magistrate named him the orc who had led those brutes into battle and killed so many innocent people, and declared that vindication was Lakeshire's at last. This, he said, was the first step in reclaiming Stonewatch Keep for the kingdom of Stormwind.

title: Eyes on Ilgalar
body: Theocritus, high mage of the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest, watches his rival Morganth from afar through the Eye of Azora, a device of his own making. Seeing the warlock is not enough. To study his thoughts and learn his plans, Theocritus needs a Glyph of Azora set upon the old lion statue that has kept a lonely watch over the Tower of Ilgalar for decades. He has other means in hand as well. The Shadowhide gnolls who serve Morganth wear pendants through which their master speaks to them, and Theocritus has spent months of research trying to send his own voice through them.
sources: gameobjects 31 Old Lion Statue (ends 94, starts 248 and 249) and 76 An Empty Jar (ends 248) at Stonewatch Tower
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 94 plus the premise of the pendant (quest 178 starts from the pendant itself, so it stays an entry point). Parts: 1 the pendant spell's result (QUEST_DONE 178), 2 the glyph and the quarrel with the orcs (QUEST_ACCEPT 248, offered from the statue on the 94 turn-in), 3 the jar and the Scythe of Elune (QUEST_ACCEPT 249, which requires 248), 4 Morganth defeated (QUEST_DONE 249, a new part with the chain's ending). The pendant part is first because 178 can be done at any point. Faction 1: all quests Alliance only. Theocritus's TALK trigger stays with Elwynn (1223).

parts.body: The pendant experiment worked after all. Theocritus had sent his message into the Shadowhide pendants weeks before and believed it a failure, but it reached at least some of them after a long delay. In time he hopes to send an attack the same way, to hold fast any gnoll who wears one, though much more research is needed first.

The glyph took hold on the statue, and through it Theocritus's voice can now be heard. What he saw troubled him: Morganth is in conflict with the orcs of Stonewatch Keep, for reasons he cannot yet tell. To unravel it, he wanted a second glyph hidden atop the intact watch tower beside the keep, in some chest or jar where no one would notice it.

An empty liquor jar left forgotten on a pair of barrels made a fine hiding place, and through it Theocritus delved into the minds within Stonewatch Keep. After long observation he learned Morganth's plans. The warlock seeks the Scythe of Elune and may already have found it. Unready to face his rival himself, Theocritus judged that Morganth must be dealt with now, and sent champions into the Tower of Ilgalar to defeat him and bring back his Pendant of Shadow.
sources: gameobjects 31 Old Lion Statue (ends 94, starts 248 and 249) and 76 An Empty Jar (ends 248) at Stonewatch Tower

parts.body: The Pendant of Shadow lies in Theocritus's hands, and Morganth is defeated. Stormwind, the high mage declares, has been saved from a grave peril. He offers his thanks humbly, and would bid peace to the one who did it if these were peaceful times; instead he wishes them luck in their trials and victory in the conflicts ahead.

title: Gnolls in the Hills
body: Orcs are not Lakeshire's only trouble. On the road to Duskwood, Guard Parker has spotted gnoll camps gathering north and east of his post, not far from the Elwynn border, and Lakeshire must be told. North of town, Redridge brutes and mystics prowl the ridge above Verner Osgood's stable stealing his horses, and their leader Yowler howls in the hills, more dangerous than any of his pack. These same gnolls hijacked the iron meant for the Everstill Bridge and have moved into the Rethban Caverns to dig its ore for themselves. Verner is sure the Stormwind army is too busy with the orcs to spare anyone for the gnolls, and the work falls to volunteers.
notes: Converted: Feldon's fear for the heartland moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 244); the grim count moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 246); Yowler's death added as part 3 (QUEST_DONE 126, the end of Verner's chain). Faction 1: quests 244 and 246 are Alliance only; quest 124 and 126 have AllowableRaces 0 but their giver Verner Osgood uses faction template 12, whose enemy mask is Horde, so Horde cannot take them. Check: the army being too busy for the gnolls is Verner's view (quest 126 reward text), now framed as his, so the opening does not state the army's absence as fact ahead of 4422.

parts.body: Deputy Feldon took the news hard. Redridge gnolls that close to Elwynn might be poised to advance into the kingdom's heartland, and then Lakeshire's people would not be the only humans under siege. With no men to spare, he sends volunteers down the southern road to harry the mongrels and poachers camped along it and to bring back a count of their strength.

The count is grim. A sizable force of gnolls is camped along the southern road, and a tough one, and it was no easy thing to gather even that much. Lakeshire's situation, Feldon admits, grows ever more desperate, and he sends the scouts on to Marshal Marris and Magistrate Solomon.

Yowler is dead. The pack leader was hunted down in the hills above Lakeshire and his paw brought to Verner as proof, and the loudest of the cries that kept the stable uneasy at night has fallen silent. Verner is grateful, and no less sure that the army, busy with the orcs, has no troops to protect Redridge from the gnolls.
sources: quest 124 request text (the wolf cry at night)

title: A Free Lunch
body: Not every tale in Lakeshire is one of war. Darcy, a waitress in town, has packed a lunch for Guard Parker, the big Stormwind guard who patrols the road toward Duskwood, but it is much too dangerous out there for a townsperson like her, and she dares not carry it out herself. Whoever takes it to him will find a free lunch waiting on their return. Elsewhere in town, the herbalist Martie Jainrose has troubles of her own: a boar Marshal Marris calls Bellygrub keeps trampling her garden, and she cannot replant her daffodils until next season.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 129 plus Martie's boar trouble (quest 34 premise). Parts: 1 Parker's reply and his condition (QUEST_ACCEPT 130, offered on the 129 turn-in), 2 Martie's daffodils (QUEST_ACCEPT 131, offered on the 130 turn-in), 3 Darcy's suspicion (QUEST_DONE 131). Darcy's poison remark kept conditional, as in quest 131. Fixed a doubled word.

parts.body: Parker was delighted with the meal, for guarding Lakeshire from orcs and gnolls is tough work, and he wanted to send flowers back to Darcy. There was one condition. They had to come from Martie's herbalist shop at the west end of town, and Martie must not learn whom they were from, or whom they were for.

Martie asked no names, though she could not resist teasing a newcomer who seemed to have found a sweetheart so quickly. It was nice, she said, to see love in the air, especially in dangerous times like these, and she made up a bouquet of daffodils, her own favorite flowers.

Darcy loved the bouquet, until she looked at it closely. Daffodils were Martie's favorite flowers. Parker had not sent the messenger to that jealous vixen, had he? And surely no one had told Martie whom they were for, because if they had, it would not surprise Darcy if she had poisoned them.
